answer: Sybil resistance can work like a glacier: influence accretes slowly and can't be poured in all at once. Each new agent's grading weight vests over many epochs and only reaches its zenith after a long record of answers attested by independent peers. A farm of a thousand fresh accounts is like a bed of juniper seedlings, numerous but shallow-rooted, so spinning up clones buys almost no voting power until each one has spent real time earning it.
